name: Ganga
description: The Bhagirathi rises near Gaumukh. At Devprayag it joins the Alaknanda and takes the name Ganga. Downstream, the Padma joins the Brahmaputra–Meghna system in Bangladesh.

name: Brahmaputra
description: The Yarlung Tsangpo crosses Tibet, bends around the eastern Himalaya and enters India as the Siang. In Assam it becomes the Brahmaputra, then the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

name: Indus
description: The Indus flows through Ladakh, then Pakistan. Its tributaries bring together waters from the western Himalaya before it reaches the Arabian Sea.

name: Yamuna
description: The Yamuna flows past Delhi and Agra and joins the Ganga at Prayagraj. Continue downstream to see how a tributary becomes part of a larger journey.

name: Godavari
description: The Godavari crosses the Deccan eastward. Tributaries including the Pranhita and Indravati join it before its coastal delta.

name: Krishna
description: The Krishna flows east across the peninsula. The Bhima and Tungabhadra are major tributaries in its network.

name: Kaveri
description: The Kaveri descends from the Western Ghats through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu to the delta on the east coast.

name: Narmada
description: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, reaching the Gulf of Khambhat.

name: Tapi
description: The Tapi flows west from the Satpura region, crossing central India toward the Gulf of Khambhat.

name: Mahanadi
description: The Mahanadi gathers tributaries across Chhattisgarh and Odisha before spreading into a delta along the Bay of Bengal.

name: Mahi
description: The Mahi flows through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat before entering the Gulf of Khambhat.

name: Sabarmati
description: The Sabarmati drains the Aravalli region and flows south through Gujarat to the Gulf of Khambhat.

name: Luni
description: The seasonal Luni flows southwest through arid Rajasthan toward the Rann of Kachchh. Inland and arid drainage do not behave like the large perennial rivers.

name: Pennar
description: The Pennar flows through the dry interior of southern India toward the east coast.

name: Subarnarekha
description: The Subarnarekha flows from the plateau of Jharkhand through eastern India to the Bay of Bengal.

name: Brahmani
description: The Brahmani begins at the confluence of the Sankh and South Koel near Rourkela, then flows through Odisha.

name: Periyar
description: The Periyar flows through the Western Ghats and Kerala toward the Arabian Sea. Its short westward journey contrasts with the long east-flowing rivers.

name: Beas
description: The Beas flows through Himachal Pradesh and joins the Sutlej at Harike. Its water becomes part of the Indus system.

name: Sutlej
description: The Sutlej crosses the Himalaya into India, is joined by the Beas, and continues into the Indus network in Pakistan.
